rationale: I read the complete held EO 7980 (3 FR 2359, Oct. 4, 1938, signed Sept. 29, 1938; the held extract also carries EO 7981 on Civil Service Schedule B, which is a separate order): under sec. 22 of EO 6166 it orders that the transfers, consolidations and eliminations contemplated by sec. 4 of EO 6166, together with the operation of the other provisions of EO 6166 so far as they relate to sec. 4, 'be further delayed until December 31, 1938, with respect to the function of disbursement now exercised by United States Marshals under the Department of Justice'. It has no other operative clause, no extension mechanism and no savings clause. The cited TERM record (stated end 1938-12-31, kind until_event, scope EO:7980#whole) is taken from the app-executive-orders text copy; I checked that the identical words appear in the official Federal Register extract (fr-originals EO_7980.txt) and rely on that reading, not on the copy, which is never an original. On its own term the postponement stopped operating at the end of December 31, 1938, and nothing else in the order survives it. D6 self-check: the history has one observation (Amends: EO 6166) and no events. A search of all held texts for 7980 finds no amendment or extension of EO 7980 itself; later postponements of the same EO 6166 sec. 4 function were separate orders (not held under that wording), and EO 8455 (5 FR 2420, June 29, 1940) sec. 3 finally transferred the marshals' disbursement functions to the Department of Justice, which confirms the scheme was closed out. A later separate postponement could not revive EO 7980. Residual risk: whether an unheld order amended the date of EO 7980 rather than issuing a new postponement. Provisional NO hypothesis only.
